Article Title: Of 97 left out in Goa, 88 are back, 3 others are Portuguese citizens: EC
Article Text:
Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents.

NEW DELHI: The office of the Goa chief electoral officer on Thursday said 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. However, he also revealed that three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India."In respect of voters who are currently residing outside India, officials are making efforts to establish and maintain contact with them for necessary action," the CEO said while sharing the status report on the 97 cases on X.Section 9 of the Constitution disallows dual citizenship. Goans born before 1961 in former Portuguese territories, as well as their kids and grandchildren, can apply for a Portuguese passport based on a citizen card issued by the Portuguese authorities after verifying their birth/descent documents. Portugal recognises dual citizenship; however, since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.As per Sec 9 of the Citizenship Act, 1955, a person's Indian citizenship automatically ceases upon acquiring foreign citizenship.Thus, three of the Portuguese passport holders in Goa may be classified as non-citizens, making them ineligible to be enrolled as Indian electors, said a source.Incidentally, Portuguese passport holders form 3% of the cohort of 97 electors for which the Goa CEO had repeatedly written to the EC after the ERO could not add them back via ERONet, leading the ECs to also raise questions on why access for such changes was 'centralised' and not available to the field officers. The issue was further amplified by the opposition parties after The Indian Express reported on the alleged internal notes of the election commissioners in this regard.EC sources on Thursday said the due diligence by the ERO the second time around may have served the purpose of SIR, as it is aimed at eliminating ineligible persons from the voters' list. Also, the fact that the issue was detected at the ERO level proves that the absolute right to add or delete a voter, based on verification, remains with the field officers, an EC officer told TOI.
Article Summary: 88 of the 97 voters in the state whose names could not be included in the roll due to an alleged ECINet issue have been added back after their duly filled Form 6 was accepted. Three of these 97 electors are Portuguese passport holders while six others were electors currently based outside India. Since dual citizenship is not allowed in India, anybody who acquires a foreign passport must surrender his Indian passport.

The aircraft was carrying 174 passengers, including 27 children.Videos circulating on social media showed Machchhar drenched in blood, wearing an oxygen mask and lying on his back in the aircraft galley.According to Netanyahu's account, an Israeli passenger told him that the aircraft began descending sharply before the passenger and a crew member managed to enter the cockpit. NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Friday spoke to India's "hero" pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who is undergoing treatment in the UAE after being injured while resisting an attack by his Omani co-pilot.Machchhar, bleed profusely after knife attack, struggled to open the cockpit door, which led the passengers, mainly Israeli security forces and air marshals, onboard to subdue the attacker.Captain Smit gave details of his experience and what gave him courage during the incident, which is being seen as a possible hijack attempt. PM Modi applauded his bravery and wished him a quick recovery.The flydubai flight issued an emergency alert and abruptly descended thousands of feet as the incident unfolded. Israel scrambled warplanes amid concerns about a possible hijacking.The plane carrying passengers from the flight landed Wednesday evening in Israel, however, it was not clear what motivated the attack. “We are guarding the pilot,” one person said in Hebrew. In another video, passengers wept and cried out as the aircraft shook.Those who intervened “saved many lives and prevented a major disaster,” Netanyahu said, adding that Saudi Arabia arrested a pilot whose identity was not immediately shared by authorities.Just another pilot until a day ago, Machchhar became the toast of India, and the world, as acclamations and tributes streamed in Thursday from US President Donald Trump, PM Modi, President Droupadi Murmu and Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, among others, for putting his life at risk to avert a mid-air tragedy.The knife attack on Smit by the co-pilot inside the cockpit had forced the flight carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv, Israel, to make an emergency landing in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday. As a captain and line trainer, he spoke to loaders and catering staff with the same respect as fellow pilots, friends said.

Article Title: EC launches special drive to restore names dropped during SIR, BLOs to trace left-out voters
Article Text:
SIR fallout: EC orders house-to-house drive to trace voters dropped from rolls

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission has directed state poll officials to launch a special drive to immediately enrol “left-out” and new voters in areas where the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has been completed. The move comes amid allegations by the opposition parties that the electoral roll revision exercise disenfranchised crores of eligible citizens.The instructions were conveyed in an official communication issued on Thursday, following a virtual meeting with state chief electoral officers (CEOs), as cited by PTI.The drive aims to re-enrol eligible voters who were omitted or deleted during the intensive revision, while also registering first-time and “young voters”.The Commission stressed that voter registration is an ongoing process and that no eligible citizen should be disenfranchised for not being included during the SIR enumeration.Booth Level Officers (BLOs) have been instructed to cross-check the current electoral rolls with pre-SIR lists to identify electors whose names were included earlier but dropped from the final roll.BLOs will conduct house-to-house verification of all identified missing electors.Each officer will be tasked with covering 20 to 25 electors a week, with the verification drive targeted for completion within a month.BLOs will also collect Form 6 applications on the spot from newly eligible young electors and genuine left-out voters. The lists will subsequently be shared directly with Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of recognised political parties to ensure transparency.The move follows a September 26 meeting of the full Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. After the meeting, the poll panel said the declaration attached to Form 6 was meant “specifically for SIR” and that “for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.”The Election Commission has withdrawn the additional SIR-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise has been completed.The declaration has been removed from the ECINET app and portal, as well as the respective Chief Electoral Officer portals. New applicants in these states will now only have to submit the regular statutory Form 6 for voter enrolment.In states and Union territories where the SIR exercise is still underway, the additional declaration remains available on the ECINET portal. Under the declaration, new applicants are required to provide details linking themselves, their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls prepared during an earlier SIR.
Article Summary: The drive aims to re-enrol eligible voters who were omitted or deleted during the intensive revision, while also registering first-time and ‘young voters’ The Election Commission has withdrawn the additional SIR-related declaration attached to Form 6 in states where the electoral roll revision exercise has been completed.

Article Title: Chita Andolan is back: Why are Madhya Pradesh's Panna villagers protesting against Ken-Betwa project
Article Text:

What is happening in Madhya Pradesh's Panna?

Several women and other protesters had fallen ill after staying in water and rain for several days, with some suffering from wounds on their feet and other skin-related problems. (ANI photo)

So why are the protesters back?

For thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project, it has become a battle over land, forests, livelihoods and identity.

Affected families have staged some of the country's most striking demonstrations, standing waist-deep in river water, laying beside symbolic funeral pyres and even climbed symbolic gallows.

What is the project aiming to accomplish?

Remember the unnerving visuals from Chita Andolan in Madhya Pradesh? Displaced Tribals sleeping on pyres, standing in water for their compensation. The unique protest is back and in its 20th day with agitators battling rain, waterlogging, lathicharge and general apathy by the authorities.Activist Amit Bhatnagar, Jai Kisan Sangathan leader, who has been on a hunger strike for the past four days, was arrested on Wednesday as protesters demonstrated chita, jal, sooli, mitti, bhook (pyre, water, gallows, soil, hunger) other forms of satyagraha.Bhatnagar accused the Panna administration of suppressing the agitation by lathicharging protesters, including women.Speaking to TOI before his arrest, Bhatnagar said, "For the past three days, the police have been bringing along people dressed in plain clothes, who misbehaved with women, entered their homes and even took away people’s phones which have still not been returned. When we approach the police, they ask who took the phones. How are people supposed to identify every face and find out who took them?""There is an atmosphere of fear in the villages. If we say anything, they start resorting to lathi-charge and filing false cases against the protesters," he added.“I am courting arrest because democracy is being murdered. Are we not even allowed to protest peacefully? We are putting ourselves through hardship to raise our concerns, but instead of listening to us, they have cut off the electricity and water. Even the British never did this. ”The latest protest follows a 15-day agitation in July, led largely by tribal women, after which the administration had assured protesters that eligible and genuinely displaced families would be transparently included in compensation and rehabilitation lists.However, the protesters claimed that they did not get the promised compensation. Also, their houses were now inundated, with two to three feet of water entering homes in several villages which now stand waterlogged including Mandalia, Tapariya and Kuwarpur."The families whose houses have been submerged are so poor that they have been forced to continue living there, or put up one makeshift shelter next to another, and then another. Earlier, the water would rise by half a foot at a time. But this time there was heavy rain on the 26th and 27th of September, followed by a 24-hour red alert, leaving them with no time to move. The villages turned into islands,” said Bhatnagar.The protesters claim that the compensation process remains incomplete, with several families receiving only Rs 5 lakh despite the government announcing a Rs 12.5-lakh package.They are also opposing the compensation conditions, which makes several tribals ineligible for relief.“The cut-off date under Section 11 has been set as 2018, which means people who are now 25-26 years old have received nothing. Those who are older are getting only Rs 5 lakh. What are families with eight or 10 children supposed to do?" asked Bhatnagar, adding that they were not against development projects, but that this development should not come at the cost of the rights of tribals.Bhatnagar pointed to Section 38 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which he said raised concerns about any displacement or submergence taking place before compensation and rehabilitation obligations had been fulfilled.“Villages and homes are now submerged. Houses have started collapsing and water has entered them. Yet, Section 38 of the 2013 law says that compensation for an irrigation project should be paid six months before submergence. If the houses were submerged two months ago, compensation should have been paid eight months earlier,” he said.The authorities, on the other hand, claim that they have been conducting fresh surveys and distributing compensation to affected families. TOI reached out to Chhatarpur district magistrate and is still awaiting a response from the administration.The Majhgawan dam project aims to transfer surplus water from Ken river to Betwa through the Daudhan Dam, a network of tunnels and a 221-km canal. It is supposed to address water shortages in drought-prone Bundelkhand region that spans across Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.The project traces back to a plan introduced in 1980 and cleared in 2021 to connect the rivers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid its foundation stone in December 2024.The project is expected to improve agricultural output, curb migration and strengthen groundwater recharge through the revival of traditional Chandela-era ponds.
Article Summary: The Ken-Betwa River Linking Project is India's first river-linking initiative. The project aims to transform the drought-prone Bundelkhand region through irrigation, drinking water supply and power generation. Thousands of tribal families living in the path of the project are protesting against the project.

Article Title: Flydubai flight drama: How Indian pilot Smit Machchhar stopped Omani co-pilot from crashing plane
Article Text:
The captain has years of experience and was a SpiceJet pilot till 2022

What happened inside the cockpit

Flydubai confirms incident

NEW DELHI: An Indian pilot has been identified as the captain who helped prevent a flydubai passenger plane from crashing after his co-pilot allegedly tried to take control of the aircraft during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media reports and an Israeli journalist.The Indian pilot has been identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai, who intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it.The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.Machchhar is an experienced commercial pilot with more than 13 years of flying experience on Boeing 737 aircraft. He has been a captain with flydubai since June 2022, having previously spent 11 years with SpiceJet, where he served as a senior commander and Line Training Captain.During his time at SpiceJet, Machchhar reportedly flew more than 9,500 hours, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command, and served as a Line Training Captain from November 2020 to June 2022. His experience includes pilot training and mentoring, crew resource management, flight standards and compliance, and B737 NG and MAX operations.The incident unfolded aboard flydubai Flight FZ1073 on Wednesday, with the Boeing 737 sending emergency signals before making an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. The flight was carrying around 180 Israeli passengers, all of whom were reported safe.Also read: Passengers recall harrowing ordeal on flight that nearly crashed The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv was flying over Jordan when it transmitted an emergency signal, followed by another signal indicating possible unlawful interference.Israeli officials said the emergency signals followed a physical altercation between the two pilots. Reuters reported that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit. Both pilots were later hospitalised after the aircraft landed in Tabuk.Israeli media reports said the suspected attacker attempted to take control of the aircraft and force it into a descent. Passengers reportedly heard screaming and saw blood inside the cockpit.Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft plunging rapidly from around 34,000 feet to about 20,000 feet, with Reuters reporting a drop of nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the aircraft stabilised.The aircraft was initially treated as a possible hijacking, prompting Israeli fighter jets to be scrambled. The Israeli prime minister's office later said the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking.Israeli media reports have described the incident as a possible attempted suicide or deliberate crash, while Israeli officials cited by Reuters said they were assessing it as a possible attempted "terror attack". Reuters also reported that officials did not believe the incident was related to a mental-health issue.Later, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilots became involved in a physical altercation as the flight approached Israel. “During the flight as they approached the country one of the pilots stabbed the other pilot,” Netanyahu said in a video address.“Apparently he tried to crash the plane with its occupants.” Netanyahu added “almost all” passengers were Israelis, with some passengers and crew members breaking into the cockpit and subduing the attacker. “I spoke with one of the Israeli passengers. He told me that the plane went into a spin and began to dive. He told me that somehow he managed to break into the cockpit with one of the crew members and together they neutralized the stabbing pilot while he was trying to sabotage the aircraft’s systems,” Netanyahu said. “Another air crew that was on the plane entered the cockpit and managed to stabilize the plane,” he added. He also praised those who intervened, saying: “I salute these heroes who showed exceptional resourcefulness and courage.They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster.”Also read: Israel security minister on flydubai cockpit incident Flydubai has confirmed that Flight FZ1073 experienced an incident during its journey from Dubai to Tel Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely."Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities. Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available," the airline said.Read more: Passenger's mother says pilot tried to kill co-pilot on Flydubai flight The airline has not publicly confirmed the identities or nationalities of the pilots or provided details about what happened inside the cockpit.The investigation is continuing, with Israeli authorities examining the circumstances of the cockpit confrontation, the alleged attempt to take control of the aircraft and the security clearance given to the crew.
Article Summary: Indian pilot identified as Captain Smit Machchhar, based in Dubai. He intervened to stop his Omani co-pilot allegedly trying to take control of the aircraft and crash it. The Indian captain was stabbed repeatedly and drenched in blood, according to various witness reports and officials.

CHENNAI: DMK president M K Stalin on Friday issued a strong warning to the C Joseph Vijay-led TVK govt, accusing it of surrendering TN’s interests by attempting to impose Hindi in the state.In a social media post, Stalin said TN had traditionally fought against Hindi imposition by the Union govt, but the ruling TVK administration was now carrying out the same agenda. Article Title: 'He has good ideas': Putin lauds PM Modi's peace push to end Russia-Ukraine war
Article Text:
Putin says PM Modi ‘constantly raises’ need to end Ukraine conflict

Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday lauded Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s efforts to seek an end to the Ukraine conflict, saying that he has “good ideas” for achieving a peaceful resolution."Prime Minister Narendra Modi is one of those world leaders who, despite our very good and even friendly relations, personal good relations, constantly raises the question and asks the question about putting an end to the conflict in Ukraine," Putin said.Asked about the issue at the Valdai Club forum, Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been actively working to find mutually acceptable solutions to the Ukraine conflict."He has an avid interest and very good ideas aimed at finding mutually acceptable solutions. In that sense, naturally, the Prime Minister takes a neutral position but with an interest in the end of the conflict. I think it's my duty to say that directly. And we are thankful to the Prime Minister for his ideas," Putin said.Putin thanked PM Modi for his efforts and continued support for resolving the Ukraine conflict through dialogue."We are thankful for his desire to put an end to this conflict through peaceful means and as soon as possible," he added.Prime Minister Modi and Putin last met in September on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where they discussed strengthening trade ties, including the implementation of the Programme for Economic Cooperation 2030, along with cooperation in infrastructure, energy, technology, defence and culture.PM Modi has repeatedly called for peace, stressing that India has maintained a principled and humanitarian approach to the Russia-Ukraine conflict."India has maintained a principled and humanitarian stance on the conflict which is equally appreciated by both President Putin and President Zelenskyy. In line with this, both the leaders spoke to me to share their perspectives on the developments related to the conflict. I reiterated India's principled and consistent stand and encouraged dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict," the Prime Minister said during an interview with Japanese news outlet 'The Yomiuri Shimbun' while on a visit to the country in August.Responding to a question on India’s role in peace efforts between the two countries, Prime Minister Modi said, "I have already indicated India's willingness to support meaningful efforts aimed at achieving a peaceful resolution of the conflict. I believe, by virtue of our good relations with both sides, including key stakeholders, we can strengthen efforts dedicated to the restoration of an early and lasting peace in Ukraine. "This comes as Putin reiterated Moscow’s long-standing position that Russia has no plans to attack European countries, while warning that it would respond to any aggression with “all weapons” at its disposal.He also accused Western countries, particularly in Europe, of escalating tensions by discussing preparations for a possible war with Moscow, conducting military drills in the Baltic Sea and seizing Russian vessels.European leaders and intelligence agencies have warned that Russia could be capable of launching an attack on another country within the next few years, particularly if it emerges victorious from the war in Ukraine.
Article Summary: Putin says PM Modi ‘constantly raises’ need to end Ukraine conflict. PM Modi has repeatedly called for peace, stressing that India has maintained a principled and humanitarian approach to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Putin reiterated Moscow’s long-standing position that Russia has no plans to attack European countries, while warning that it would respond to any aggression with “all weapons”

Article Title: ‘Fewer workers, more CM aspirants’: CM Mann takes swipe at Punjab Congress leadership crisis
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Thursday took a swipe at the ongoing turmoil in the Congress state unit and said that even the new state president will not be able to unite the party leaders.Mann said that the Congress has fewer party workers but more leaders who aspire to become chief minister.“A new president will be appointed, but even the new president will not be able to unite the Congress leaders. After the new president comes, the fight amongst them will further intensify,” Mann said.“The Congress has fewer 'karyakartas' but more leaders who aspire to become CM, not for the well-being of the people but for satisfying their lust for power,” he added.This comes after the Congress high command replaced Amrinder Singh Raja Warring as the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief ahead of the Punjab assembly polls.Although Warring declined to comment on the development, he confirmed it by changing his X bio to “former Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee President”.The move comes after months of infighting within the Punjab Congress, which intensified after the party high command decided on July 1 to retain Warring as the state unit chief.A section of leaders led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi had opposed Warring’s continuation and sought his removal. Leaders aligned with the Channi camp also stayed away from party programmes led by Warring.According to PTI, the Congress general secretary and Punjab in-charge held a series of meetings with state leaders before submitting his report to the party high command on the proposed leadership change.The high command subsequently informed Warring of its decision, party sources told PTI, adding that the Congress is now looking to appoint a leader who can bring different factions together ahead of the 2027 assembly polls.Warring had also faced criticism from sections of the party over the Congress’ electoral performance in Punjab and his leadership.In August, he defended himself against criticism over the party’s decline in the 2022 assembly elections, questioning attempts to hold him responsible for the loss.
Article Summary: Mann said that the Congress has fewer party workers but more leaders who aspire to become chief minister. This comes after the Congress high command replaced Amrinder Singh Raja Warring as the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) chief ahead of the Punjab assembly polls.

Article Title: Few responsibilities in a civilised society are as profound as that entrusted to a doctor, says SC, while cancelling Ramesh Mhatre’s bail
Article Text:
The SC order available on Thursday extended the deadline to complete the trial.





MUMBAI: “The legitimacy of public authority ultimately rests not upon the power to command, but upon the obligation to remain within the bounds of law and serve the nation. It is this distinction that must remain inviolable in a constitutional democracy,” the Supreme Court said in its reasoned order by which it had on Sept 28 set aside the Bombay HC order of bail to Ramesh Mhatre, the 73 year old municipal corporator in the July 6 Kalyan Dombivli Municipal Corporation doctors’ assault case in a Dombivli hospital.The SC order available on Thursday extended the deadline to complete the trial. The HC had set a 3 month deadline to complete the trial for the magistrate in Kalyan.The SC made it six months from the date of presentation of its order and while cancelling Mhatre’s bail in the State’s plea said he is at liberty to apply for it in case of any change of circumstances.The SC noted that assaults on doctors was being reported across states and said, “While each such incident must necessarily be examined on its own facts and in accordance with law, the recurrence of allegations involving elected representatives assuming, or seeking to assume, authority beyond that conferred by law is a matter which cannot be viewed with indifference.”SC bench of justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta observed that an elected office carries with it a corresponding obligation to respect the rule of law and the institutions through which grievances are to be addressed.“The authority derived from the electoral mandate cannot be permitted to become a substitute for the authority of law,” the bench stressed.The state had filed an appeal and through advocate Shreerang Varma argued for cancellation of Mhatre’s bail.Senior counsel Siddharth Dave for Mhtatre had opposed.The SC accepted the State’s plea and disposing it off invoked a verse from the Suśruta Saṃhitā which it said eloquently expressed an enduring truth of how “efficacy of medical care is inseparable from the trust and respect reposed in the doctors and nurses.”“Its literal sense, the verse conveys that a physician does not succeed in a house where he is not respected; where the physician is respected, his treatment succeeds. Though expressed in the language of an ancient medical tradition, the principle underlying the verse retains undiminished relevance even today,” said the 36 page judgment authored by Justice Mehta.“Few responsibilities in a civilised society are as profound as that entrusted to a doctor,” the judgment underscored.“The special place accorded to the medical profession flows from the very nature of the service it renders to humanity. It concerns human life, human dignity and the alleviation of human suffering. A doctor is, therefore, required to bring to the discharge of his or her duties not merely knowledge and technical competence, but also sound judgment, patience, composure and compassion. The responsibility is consequently of a character that extends beyond the mere provision of a professional service. ”The SC said, "It is this unique character of the profession that distinguishes the relationship between a doctor and a patient from an ordinary commercial or service relationship. A patient does not merely engage a professional for the performance of a task; he places his health and, in serious cases, his very life in the hands of the doctor. The relationship is thus founded upon a degree of trust that cannot be measured merely by the professional service rendered or the remuneration received. ""The ancient Roman Stoic philosopher Lucius Annaeus Seneca aptly expressed the thought, while the physician is paid for his professional service, gratitude remains owed for the kindness and care that transcend the service itself. The observation aptly recognises that the confidence, reassurance and humanity accompanying medical care form an integral part of the relationship between the doctor and the patient," it added."A doctor cannot reasonably be expected to exercise sound and independent judgement while labouring under the apprehension of physical violence, intimidation or coercion," the SC observed and added, "The safety and dignity of the medical professional are consequently not matters of personal privilege. They are the safeguards which serve the larger public interest in ensuring that medical care is rendered with the concentration, composure and judgement that the profession demands. "But, it also noted that it "does not place medical professionals beyond scrutiny or accountability. A patient or his family remains entitled to question the treatment provided, complain of negligence or delay, seek investigation into an adverse outcome and pursue such remedies as are available in law. Indeed, the availability of these lawful avenues is essential to ensuring accountability within the medical profession. "The SC also said, "What the law cannot countenance is the substitution of these remedies by threat, violence and coercion. Physical violence, intimidation or coercion cannot become a means of expressing dissatisfaction with medical treatment, securing compliance with a demand or raising grievance for an adverse medical outcome. A grievance, however genuine, does not confer a licence to resort to violence.""To permit such conduct would not merely imperil the individual doctor. It would undermine the very conditions in which medical professionals are required to make decisions upon which the life and health of patients may depend. Any patronage to such activities would alter the civil society in one run by outlaws," it further said.Police arrested Mhatre on July 8 for allegedly slapping and punching a doctor and assaulting a resident medical officer. A local court granted him bail on July 14, while he was in a hospital.He was released but on July 18 the HC acting chief justice RV Ghuge led bench took up the matter suo motu and staying the bail order for all four, directed Mhatre to surrender. He did on July 19.The HC eventually granted him bail on August 7 and the ACJ had also said, “In a democracy an elected representative is by the people and for the people. If the elected representative is accused of assaulting his own voters, such a situation is bound to dent the fabric of democracy in this country and erode public confidence.’’The SC gave Mhatre till October 5 to surrender.Before the SC, the maximum sentence under the law is five years’ imprisonment for the main offence in the case and there was no obstruction caused in the trial caused, Mhatre’s counsel also submitted.While acknowledging the concerns raised by the bench, the counsel submitted that as a “criminal case” evidence had to form the basis of the outcome.The SC said, “We direct the Special Fast Track Court, constituted pursuant to the directions of the high court, shall endeavour to conclude the trial as expeditiously as possible and, in any event, not later than six months from the date of presentation of the present order.”And added, “We also direct the prosecution to carefully assess the list of witnesses proposed to be examined and, wherever permissible in law, to curtail or dispense with the examination of such witnesses whose evidence may not be essential for the just adjudication of the case, so as to ensure that the trial proceeds expeditiously without compromising the fairness of the proceedings.”
Article Summary: The Supreme Court had on Sept 28 set aside the Bombay HC order of bail to Ramesh Mhatre, the 73 year old municipal corporator. The HC had set a 3 month deadline to complete the trial for the magistrate in Kalyan. The SC made it six months from the date of presentation of its order.

UJJAIN: A large group of people clashed with police in Ujjain at the spot where a portion of the Shahi Masjid was demolished as part of a road-widening project, news agency ANI reported on Monday.Heavy police force remains deployed in the area.The situation reportedly turned tense when some unidentified individuals began pelting stones in the area. Police personnel intervened to bring the situation under control and fired tear-gas shells to disperse the crowd.The confrontation took place as the Ujjain Municipal Corporation started removing the mosque portion falling within the proposed road alignment for the widening project ahead of Simhastha 2028.Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel are also present at the spot.Earlier, Madhya Pradesh chief minister Mohan Yadav intitaed various develoment works in Ujjain with the demolition activity carried out at his ancestral home.272 structures have been marked for demolition as part of a road-widening project in Ujjain ahead of the Simhastha 2028 fair.Speaking on the occasion, Yadav said the demolition of his childhood home carried personal significance, but was necessary for the larger cause."This is the place where I grew up, playing and running around, and now I am stepping forward to dismantle it with my own hands. It certainly has an emotional impact. However, if it is necessary for the administration and essential for the Simhastha, then this sacrifice must be made. I am satisfied that we are all doing this together," he said.He added that the gesture was meant to set an example for residents whose properties were also being affected by the project."The entire state and the country are watching this. People are demolishing their homes willingly and happily, dedicating themselves to the cause so that others may benefit greatly," he said.Ujjain Municipal Corporation Chairperson Kalawati Yadav explained the scale of preparations underway for the upcoming religious gathering, as it is one of the biggest spiritual gatherings that happens once every 12 years."In 2028, Ujjain will host the Simhastha Mela, one of the world's largest spiritual gatherings, held every 12 years on the banks of the Shipra River. With millions of devotees expected, road widening has become essential," she said.The road-widening initiative forms part of the broader infrastructure overhaul being undertaken in Ujjain to accommodate the massive influx of pilgrims expected during the Simhastha Mela in 2028.
