NEW DELHI: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student on the university campus. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. Several policemen were injured.The university has suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice. Heavy police deployment has been made on the campus, while students have started leaving for their homes.Classes suspended, exams postponedFollowing the violence, LPU suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28 and postponed mid-term examinations until further notice.The administration appealed to students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.Several rounds of talks between protesting students and the university management remained inconclusive.Vice Chancellor Sandhu assured students that their genuine grievances would be addressed.The protesters demanded that LPU Founder-Chancellor Ashok Mittal, who is also a BJP Rajya Sabha MP, visit the protest site and assure them that their concerns would be resolved. They also sought that access to the University Management System not be blocked and that students not be victimised for participating in the protest.A large police force led by ADGP M F Farooqui entered the LPU campus after the violence escalated. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night, Farooqui said.“We will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control. I cannot provide further details at this moment. To the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe... The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace. ..,” he said.Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances in the hostels were rumours and that all hostels had been checked.“First of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal. Other matters will be resolved through discussions with the students... Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern,” Singh said.DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said the situation had been brought under control and that traffic movement on NH-44 would soon be restored.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has directed strict action against those responsible for the unrest at Lovely Professional University (LPU), the Chief Minister’s Office said.Mann also directed Director General of Police Gaurav Yadav to visit the spot and assess the situation.The protest began near Girls' Hostel-3 around 1 am on Sunday after students alleged that a female student had been raped by a plumber three days earlier. They also claimed the hostel warden had been informed but no action was taken.The protesters blocked NH-44 outside the university from around 8 am, causing long queues of stranded vehicles. Police later attempted to clear the blockade, but students allegedly threw water bottles at them and clashed with personnel.Police resorted to a mild lathi charge, following which students moved towards the campus and continued to pelt stones at police vehicles. Two police vehicles were set on fire, while four to five vehicles were damaged, according to Jalandhar Rural SSP Harvinder Singh Virk.Viral videos showed damaged property, vehicles and an ATM kiosk on the campus. Some students were also seen climbing onto a decommissioned MiG-23UM aircraft and a military tank installed on the premises.A truck driver, Vikas Yadav, said, “We have been stranded since 7 AM; there is no sign of things opening up yet... We are extremely distressed... We have had to abandon our vehicles and flee...”Police said an FIR had been registered against an unknown person based on a complaint by the students and a special investigation team had been formed.Singla said the girl was staying in Hostel No. 3 and had returned to her home after students alleged that no action had been taken on the matter. He said the investigation would involve student representatives.“We will analyse forensic samples, CCTV camera footage, call records, etc., before reaching a conclusion,” Singla said.The DIG also said students had demanded that the hostel staff comprise only women, adding that the management would address the demand.Asked about another death, Singla said a female student from Telangana studying at LPU had died by suicide 15 days earlier. “If the students say that there was foul play, action will be taken,” he said.LPU Vice Chancellor Jaspal Singh Sandhu said the university was not aware of any such rape incident but would cooperate with the investigation.LPU management has denied the rape allegations, with Registrar Monica Gulati saying certain “anti-social elements” were spreading “false, baseless and fabricated” claims.The university released a video featuring three female students identified as residents of Room No. 504 of the hostel. In the video, the students said no rape had taken place in their room and asked police and other students not to disturb them.Gulati introduced the video by saying, “I would like you to hear what the girls residing in room number 504 of GH3 told us.”The first student said, “So, we are the residents of room number 504. Nothing of that sort happened in our room; we have been living here for the past two months. Please, police and students, do not bother us. Nothing like that happened in our room, and we are not involved in this at all.”The second student said, “We have been extremely distressed today, and if we face further trouble, we will involve our parents. Please do not harass us.”The third added, “And the police should also stop coming to our room repeatedly; otherwise, we will call our parents.”Gulati later said, “The only conclusion to be drawn from all this is that anti-social elements and individuals with vested interests are behind this.”The opposition Congress criticised the AAP government over the law and order situation in Punjab.“What is happening at LPU is deeply concerning. If students have serious questions or concerns about any incident, they deserve transparent, impartial and time-bound answers, not rumours or suppression. The violence is a testament to the failed law and order situation in Punjab,” state Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring said.“NH-44 has been blocked since the morning, yet not a single representative from the AAP government has bothered to meet the students and hear their grievances,” Warring said.
Article Summary: Students of Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara went on a rampage on Sunday, vandalising property and blocking NH-44 during protests over claims that an outsider raped a female student. The protests later turned violent as students clashed with police, damaged and set fire to vehicles, and pelted stones at security personnel. More than 2,000 personnel have been deployed to maintain security through the night.

Article Title: 'Odd-hour guests, security risk': Noida's Supernova society bans Airbnb, Oyo, Booking.com rentals after host gate-ramming video
Article Text:
Residents of Supernova in Sector 94 have expressed concern over short-term rentals affecting security in their complex.





NOIDA: Short-term rentals listed on Airbnb, Oyo and Booking.com have come under the scanner at Supernova in Sector 94, with the residents’ association warning flat owners and tenants against renting out homes to guests for brief stays.The Supernova Apartment Owners’ Association has circulated a notice saying residents who list or rent out flats on these platforms for short-term stays could face legal action. The association said the responsibility would rest with the respective flat owners or tenants.The move comes days after a bed-and-breakfast operator was arrested for allegedly driving through a security barrier at the complex after guards stopped him from entering through the main gate.The incident, which was recorded by security guards and later circulated on social media, has intensified concerns among residents over the movement of short-stay guests and security at the mixed-use complex.Naresh K Nandwani of the Supernova AOA said the project has three towers — Nova East, Nova West and Spira Tower. Nova East and Nova West are fully residential and together have 582 units, while Spira Tower has a mixed-use component.Around 200 flats between the 19th and 43rd floors of Spira Tower are used commercially, including for short-term accommodation, Nandwani said.All three towers share a common campus and gates, he said, adding that residents have raised concerns about guests entering and leaving the premises at odd hours. The association said such movement had led to nuisance and raised security concerns in the predominantly residential complex.The latest action followed an incident on Wednesday involving Sector 15 resident Tushar Sharma, who operates a short-stay accommodation in Spira.According to police, Sharma reached the complex and allegedly tried to enter through the main Supernova gate instead of the designated Spira entrance. Security guards stopped him and asked him to use the tower’s designated gate.Sharma allegedly told the guards that one of his guests had been stopped at the reception and that he needed to enter the complex to check the guest in. He allegedly assured them that he would leave after dropping the guest.When the guards did not open the gate, an argument broke out. Sharma allegedly drove his Skoda through the boom barrier.Other guards recorded the incident, and the video was later widely shared on social media. Several users tagged the police on X, following which police took cognisance of the incident and registered a case at Sector 126 police station.Sharma was arrested on Thursday under BNS sections 352 and 324(4), relating to intentional insult and mischief causing damage.Police also found six pending e-challans linked to the Skoda’s owner, amounting to around Rs 36,000. The vehicle is registered in Ranchi, Jharkhand, and the pending challans in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh include violations such as overspeeding and illegal parking.The action at Supernova also comes against the backdrop of the UP government’s Bed and Breakfast and Homestay Policy 2025, which seeks to bring guest facilities operating from residential properties into a formal regulatory framework.
Article Summary: Supernova Apartment Owners’ Association has circulated a notice saying residents who list or rent out flats on these platforms for short-term stays could face legal action. Move comes days after a bed-and-breakfast operator was arrested for allegedly driving through a security barrier at the complex.

Article Title: Will take China help if Centre and Manipur fail to act: Naga group
Article Text:
“If governments cannot protect vulnerable indigenous citizens, people may have to seek help from neighbours such as China,” said Southern Tangkhul Students’ Union president





GUWAHATI: Warning that neglect of Naga civilians in vulnerable Indo-Myanmar border areas could drive them to seek help from neighbouring countries, including China, a Tangkhul Naga student and civil-society group in Manipur on Tuesday demanded urgent action from the Centre and the state govt to ensure their security.“We are extremely tired at this juncture,” Tangkhul Aze Katamnao Long (TAKL), also known as Southern Tangkhul Students’ Union, president Yarchuiso Kashung said in Imphal.“If the Manipur govt and the govt of India are unwilling or unable to protect indigenous citizens, particularly those living in vulnerable border areas, people would have no option but to seek help from neighbouring countries such as China.”Kashung called for immediate action to protect Naga civilians and said, “If the chief minister is unable to protect the state and its people, he should voluntarily resign.”Expressing a sense of alienation among residents of border areas, he said, “When the Manipur state government doesn’t care, and the Central govt doesn’t care, then we, the people living in the border areas, feel like we are not part of Manipur, and not part of the central govt, not part of India.”Kashung cited recent killings of Naga civilians in Tamenglong, Senapati and Kamjong, including a 17-year-old Liangmei Naga boy, three Mao Naga civilians and four Tangkhul Naga civilians at Pilong in Kamjong, and demanded accountability.The statement comes amid continuing tensions linked to the Naga-Kuki-Zo conflict, which began in February and has claimed nearly 50 lives from both sides. Of these, 22 people — 11 from each side — were killed in the past month alone.
Article Summary: “If governments cannot protect vulnerable indigenous citizens, people may have to seek help from neighbours such as China,” said Southern Tangkhul Students’ Union president Yarchuiso Kashung. The statement comes amid continuing tensions linked to the Naga-Kuki-Zo conflict, which began in February.

Article Title: Wife locked in bedroom, leaking gas, missing caretaker: Ex-IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal’s murder in Bhopal home gets murkier
Article Text:
Nishi Agrawal found her husband Rakesh murdered in their home, with the caretaker Varun now a prime suspect





BHOPAL: In what could be a crucial piece of information amid the probe into the gruesome killing of retired IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal, his widow, Nishi, told police that she tried opening her bedroom door around 4.40 am on Wednesday, but found it locked from outside.The statement deepened the mystery around the killing after Amar, a cook employed by the family, told the cops that he spotted Varun, the 24x7 caretaker and now the absconding prime suspect, loitering outside the house around 1 am, adding that on being enquired, the latter said he came to check after hearing the sound of a door being opened.Amar said he retired to his room thereafter, while Varun proceeded towards Agrawal’s room.Nishi told the sleuths that on finding her bedroom door locked from outside, she informed Neetu, Amar’s wife who lives with him at the adjacent servants’ quarters. Neetu then informed her husband, who had a duplicate key to the house, the police said.Amar rushed in to find the main door, too, locked from outside, the sleuths said, adding that he opened it before unlocking the bedroom door.As they stepped out of the bedroom, they caught a strong whiff of leaking gas throughout the house.Proceeding to the kitchen to check, they found all LPG cylinder pipes disconnected. Amar quickly removed the cylinders to prevent a fire.They then went to Agrawal’s room, finding him in bed, the police said, adding as Nishi tried to nudge him awake, her hand was smeared with blood. She screamed aloud in horror, while Amar reached over to check for pulse. He didn’t find any.They then looked around for the caretaker but he had disappeared.ACP Ankita Khatarkar said the retired IAS officer had been discharged from hospital about 20 days ago, after recovering from a slipped disc-related condition.The sleuths, who swept the scene, said the LPG connecting pipes could well have been deliberately dislodged in a bid to set off a fire. In a crucial lead, police said the suspect was captured on a CCTV camera in Suraj Nagar around 2.15 am, appearing to be making an escape.The murder, according to the police, was likely committed sometime between 12.30 am and 2 am on Wednesday.The body, meanwhile, was sent for post-mortem and kept in a freezer at the mortuary after the procedure. Benumbed with shock after finding her husband murdered, Nishi experienced a sudden spike in blood pressure and was taken to a hospital.Ratibad police questioned the operator of the agency in Bag Sewania through which caretaker Varun was hired.According to the agency operator, Varun contacted him in Aug 2026 on a number he found online and later travelled to Bhopal from Patiala, Punjab. He told the operator that the phone number he was using belonged to his sister, police said, adding that he also submitted copies of his Aadhaar card, PAN card and police verification documents, added cops.
Article Summary: Nishi Agrawal found her husband Rakesh murdered in their home, with the caretaker Varun now a prime suspect. The statement deepened the mystery around the killing after Amar, a cook employed by the family, told the cops that he spotted Varun loitering outside the house around 1 am.

Article Title: Man in WagonR with ‘POLICE’ sticker caught stealing plant from Delhi-Dehradun Expressway
Article Text:
Police said no complaint has been received in connection with the incident so far.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think should be the priority to prevent public property theft? Increased surveillance Community involvement Stronger laws and penalties Regular patrols by authorities 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





LUCKNOW: A CCTV video showing a man allegedly stealing a plant and loading it into a WagonR bearing a “POLICE” sticker on the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway in Uttar Pradesh’s Baghpat has gone viral on social media.The footage purportedly shows the person removing a plant from the roadside and placing it inside the car.The circumstances surrounding the incident are yet to be established.Police said no complaint has been received in connection with the incident so far.Baghpat Police said, “It is to be informed that, with regard to the aforementioned case, no information or written complaint has been received at Baraut Police Station so far. The concerned NHAI department has also not provided any information to Baraut Police Station regarding the said case. The police at the station are seeking information regarding the actual status of the case. Necessary legal action will be ensured based on the information received and the facts that come to light during the investigation. ”They added that the viral video is being verified and further action will be taken based on the findings.The incident comes months after a similar plant theft was reported in Uttar Pradesh, where nearly 7,000 potted plants worth around Rs 10 lakh were allegedly stolen within 24 hours of the inauguration of Rashtra Prerna Sthal.The plants were part of a Rs 60 lakh horticulture project carried out for the event in December 2025.Lucknow Development Authority (LDA) officials said the thefts began shortly after the programme concluded.People were allegedly seen removing flower pots and leaving the area in cars and on scooters. Several videos of the incident were circulated on social media.Following the thefts, the LDA deployed 30 security personnel around the site to protect the remaining plants.Police presence was also strengthened. In some stretches, the LDA began shifting pots to Lohia Park for safekeeping.
Article Summary: CCTV video shows a man allegedly stealing a plant and loading it into a WagonR bearing a ‘POLICE’ sticker. The circumstances surrounding the incident are yet to be established. Police said no complaint has been received in connection with the incident so far.

Article Title: Bombay HC stays Sachin Waze’s bail granted by special court, issues notice on NIA appeal
Article Text:
The Justice Kulkarni-led bench issued notice to Waze and posted the matter for hearing on Oct 7.





MUMBAI: Following two recusals, a third division bench of Bombay high court comprising Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale on Wednesday stayed the bail granted by a special NIA court to former police officer Sachin Waze in the five-year-old Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case under anti-terror law UAPA.The Justice Kulkarni-led bench issued notice to Waze and posted the matter for hearing on Oct 7. Waze has spent 1,999 days in custody and is at the Thane central prison.On Feb 25, 2021, an explosives-laden SUV was found near Antilia. The NIA alleged Waze orchestrated the plot to extort wealthy individuals and project himself as a “super cop” after returning to the police force from a long suspension. Its case was that Waze allegedly used Hiran’s vehicle, fabricated theft proceedings, and planted gelatin sticks and a threat note in the vehicle. Hiran was allegedly murdered on March 4, 2021 because he knew of the conspiracy and could expose it. Waze was arrested later that month.When the matter originally came up on Wednesday as scheduled, it was listed before a division bench of Justices Bharti Dangre and Ashish Chavan. Justice Dangre asked if Waze was released or not as yet. Additional solicitor general Anil Singh for NIA said he was not.Justices Dangre and Chavan recused themselves from hearing the NIA appeal against the special trial court order of bail to Waze.Justice Dangre said she had already earlier -- in Sept 2024 -- recused and directed that Waze’s matter in the NIA case not be placed before a bench where she is a party. Her 2024 order was in a quashing plea filed by Waze.Justice Dangre said to the ASG, “We understand and appreciate your inconvenience” and expressed regret that the matter would now have to be placed before another bench.Justice Chavan—who was appointed as judge last year--too recused, saying he had as a lawyer appeared for CBI in a distinctly connected matter.On Tuesday, the HC division bench of Justices Sarang Kotwal and R R Bhonsale had recused itself when the ASG had mentioned the challenge and sought urgent hearing.After Wednesday’s recusal, the ASG mentioned the matter before HC Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi to have it assigned before another bench since a few other judges on other benches too, as lawyers, appeared for Central agencies in the case. The CJ assigned the mater to Justice Kulkarni’s bench.On Tuesday, special NIA court judge Chakor S Baviskar, granting bail to Waze, had held there was “absolutely nothing on record” to infer that industrialist Mukesh Ambani or his family were ever terrorized and repeatedly questioned the lack of statements taken and dubbed as “quite hypothetical” the allegation of any demand made by Waze of money from the Ambanis. The judge observed the SUV containing gelatin sticks was parked near Shikharkunj building on Carmichael Road, and not directly opposite Antilia on Altamont Road.In its appeal, NIA before HC said the bail order was “erroneous and illegal,” passed without going into detailed facts and circumstances, and is “completely misplaced both, on facts and law.”The appeal said the special NIA court “completely ignored the rigours of Section 43 D of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act while granting bail to the main accused (Waze) whose role is ‘central’ in character to the terror crime of this case.”Waze’s record is not “unblemished” as he submits, said the NIA, citing inquiries against him. The NIA said the “very substratum of the prosecution case is that, Waze after his reinstatement in police service after a long suspension, wanted to regain his clout.” Moreover, he was “under the compelling circumstances to collect Rs 100 crore per month from hoteliers and bar owners in Mumbai and territory, and in that process, he intended huge monetary gain for himself also and for that hatched a criminal conspiracy with other accused in this case and committed all the alleged offences. ”To allegedly execute his conspiracy to extort money from the wealthy, Waze “required a vehicle in which he could plant some explosives, park it in front of a residence of influential and wealthy industrialist or corporate tycoon and putting him under terror extort huge amounts for himself and to meet the alleged target given to him”, the NIA added.The Nia stressed Waze was in “search of easy and wealthy prey who would succumb to threat and provide any amount to avoid fatal consequence… and he chose the Ambani family.” The special NIA court said the day-to-day business of the Ambanis did not appear to have been disturbed “even for a minute” after the incident. The court said there was nothing to show whether any member of the family even came to know an explosives-laden vehicle had been parked near their residence.Justices Kulkarni and Gokhale will hear both sides on Oct 7.
Article Summary: HC stays bail granted by a special NIA court to former police officer Sachin Waze. Waze has spent 1,999 days in custody and is at the Thane central prison. The Justice Kulkarni-led bench issued notice to Waze and posted the matter for hearing on Oct 7.

Article Title: Gangotri National Park entry suspended after heavy rain, snowfall; routes to reopen in 2-3 days
Article Text:
The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.





UTTARKASHI: Following heavy rainfall and snowfall in the high-altitude Himalayan region on September 26 and 27, the Gangotri National Park administration has suspended entry into the park area until further orders, citing the safety of tourists and trekkers.Mayank Garg, Deputy Director of Gangotri National Park, told TOI that the heavy rain and snow have made various trekking routes within the park—including Gangotri-Gaumukh-Tapovan, Gartang Gali, and Kedartal—hazardous; the paths have sustained damage in several places and are currently being repaired.The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.Entry into the park area will remain prohibited until further notice to ensure the safety of tourists and trekkers.Meanwhile, Manoj Rawat, Secretary of the Uttarkashi Trekking Association, expressed concern over the sudden closure of trekking routes.He noted that tourists are facing inconvenience, as many have made advance bookings, and trekking companies have already arranged for rations, equipment, and other essential supplies.He argued that the park administration should not impose restrictions on the safer, easier routes.
Article Summary: Following heavy rainfall and snowfall in the high-altitude Himalayan region, the Gangotri National Park administration has suspended entry into the park area. The park is expected to reopen to tourists and trekkers within two to three days once all routes are restored.

Article Title: ‘Deep cut on neck’: Squabble over a book, teen slashes classmate in south Kolkata school
Article Text:
A boy whipped out a sharp object and attacked a classmate, who started bleeding profusely, triggering panic among the students (AI Imgae)

(Written with inputs from Dwaipayan Ghosh & Sumati Yengkhom in Kolkata)





KOLKATA: A 15-year-old Class IX student of a prominent south Kolkata school ended in hospital and underwent surgery after being slashed with a sharp object by a classmate inside the classroom during school hours on Wednesday.The injured teenager sustained deep cuts on his neck and multiple fingers of the left hand.According to a statement issued by the school, the incident took place around 12.29 pm in the presence of the class teacher while the class was in progress.A boy whipped out a sharp object and attacked a classmate, who started bleeding profusely, triggering panic among the students. Teachers immediately took the injured boy to the school infirmary, where nurses administered first aid before senior staff members took him to Ruby General Hospital and informed his parents.The boy who committed the assault was taken away from the classroom and counselled by school psychologists. Later, his father took him home. The school also filed a report with Gariahat police station.Additional Police Commissioner (crime) Kunal Agarwal said, “We have received a complaint from the school and are registering a case under appropriate sections of law. We have learned from the school authorities that the victim is now stable, and that the accused is an autistic child.”Ruby General Hospital said in a statement that the 15-year-old boy was first admitted to the hospital emergency. “After initial examination and resuscitation, he was taken to the OT. There was a deep laceration on the neck extending up to the face, with underlying muscle injury. Also, there was an extensor tendon injury of the left index finger along with cuts on multiple other fingers,” the statement said. “All the injuries were repaired and the patient is presently stable,” the hospital said after the surgery. The student is being treated by plastic and reconstructive surgeon Dipanjan Dey.According to teachers, the immediate trigger of the incident appears to be a squabble between the two boys over a book on Tuesday, which ended with the book getting torn. Some claimed the squabble had turned physical on Tuesday as well, but the teachers separated the two and ensured that both were counselled.After the surgery, the victim’s father told TOI, “I have not spoken to my son yet. When we dashed to the hospital, we saw a deep wound in the neck. He has been in this school since childhood. My younger child also studies in this school. He did not tell us about about any incident in school yesterday. He is usually very quiet. We are still processing this.”South Point High School in a statement said, “The incident has caused considerable distress and shock among the pupils, teachers, staff, and the wider school community. The school is deeply concerned about the physical and emotional well-being of everyone affected by the incident, particularly the children who witnessed or were otherwise impacted by what happened.”The statement added, “The school will take all necessary steps to address the emotional and psychological impact of the incident. The school remains committed to ensuring a safe, caring, and supportive environment for all its pupils and staff while dealing with the aftermath of this unfortunate incident.”A senior school official, who requested anonymity, said, “We will investigate and take not only corrective action but preventive action as well.”
Article Summary: A 15-year-old Class IX student of a prominent south Kolkata school ended in hospital and underwent surgery after being slashed with a sharp object by a classmate. The injured teenager sustained deep cuts on his neck and multiple fingers of the left hand. The boy who committed the assault was taken away from the classroom and counselled by school psychologists.

Article Title: Over 100 hearings, 22 witnesses: Wife, lover convicted in Meerut ‘blue drum’ murder case; sentencing on Oct 14
Article Text:
The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses





MEERUT: A district and sessions court in Meerut on Wednesday convicted Muskan Rastogi and her lover Sahil Shukla of murdering Muskan’s husband, merchant navy officer Saurabh Rajput, dismembering his body and concealing it in a blue plastic drum filled with cement in March 2025.The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses, with the court fixing Oct 14 for the pronouncement of the sentence.Prosecution lawyer K K Chaubey said district and sessions judge Arvind Kumar Mishra found both accused guilty of murder and destruction of evidence. Muskan and Sahil appeared before the court through video conferencing. “The court observed that the crime falls into a category that not only shreds the fabric of society but also strikes at the foundation of the husband-wife relationship,” Chaubey said. He added that when the court asked the two to make submissions on the sentence, they said they had nothing to say.Rajput’s mother, Renu Devi , was present at the court when the verdict was pronounced. “We have waited for this day for the last 18 months. We want nothing less than capital punishment for both,” she said.The case dated back to March 2025, when Muskan and Sahil killed Rajput, chopped his body into pieces, and placed the remains in a blue plastic drum filled with cement in an attempt to conceal the crime.The case came to light on March 17 after a foul smell began emanating from the drum, leading to the discovery of the body and subsequent investigation.Muskan and Sahil were arrested following the discovery and remained in custody during the trial. The gruesome manner in which Rajput’s body was concealed led to the case becoming widely known as the “blue drum murder case”. The court will hear the matter on sentencing on Oct 14.Feb 24-25, 2025: Saurabh Rajput returns to Meerut from London; Muskan’s birthday celebrated next dayMarch 4: Muskan, Sahil drug Saurabh, stab him to death, dismember body; remains packed in blue drum with cement; duo leaves for Himachal PradeshMid-March: Muskan tells maternal family about murder; police case follows; remains recovered from drum on Mar 17March 18, 2025: Muskan, Sahil arrestedMarch 19, 2025: Court sends duo to 14-day judicial custodyMay 12, 2025: Police file nearly 1,000-page chargesheet; around 34 witness statements; murder, destruction-of-evidence chargesNov 24, 2025: Muskan gives birth to girl while in custody; mother, newborn shifted to women’s barrack; Saurabh’s family seeks DNA test for paternityMar 2025-Sept 2026: Trial spans around 13 months; 22 witnesses examinedSept 17, 2026: Final arguments conclude; prosecution seeks death penalty for bothSept 30: Muskan, Sahil convicted of murder, destruction of evidence; sentencing fixed for Oct 14
Article Summary: The verdict came after more than 100 hearings and examination of 22 witnesses. The court will hear the matter on sentencing on Oct 14. The gruesome manner in which Rajput’s body was concealed led to the case becoming widely known as the ‘blue drum murder case’

Article Title: Pilot who 'never planned to fly': Mumbaikar Smit Machchhar's journey from textile course to saving 180 lives on flydubai flight
Article Text:
Captain Smit Machchhar managed to regain control of a flydubai aircraft after a co-pilot attacked him

From textile engineering to cockpit

From SpiceJet to flydubai

The flight that plunged thousands of feet





MUMBAI: Captain Smit Machchhar never grew up dreaming of flying planes. In fact, when he was 19, his career path appeared to be taking him in an entirely different direction — towards his family's textile business.An aviation seminar during a management course changed that.More than a decade later, the Mumbaikar found himself at the controls of a flydubai Boeing 737 MAX during one of the most terrifying moments of his flying career — after his co-pilot allegedly attacked him in the cockpit as the aircraft was carrying 174 passengers from Dubai to Tel Aviv.Despite being injured, Machchhar is reported to have fought back and helped prevent the aircraft from plunging further. The plane had dropped thousands of feet in a matter of seconds before passengers and crew intervened and the aircraft was eventually diverted to Saudi Arabia.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later identified Machchhar as the captain and praised his actions, saying he had helped prevent a major disaster.Machchhar's journey into aviation was anything but conventional.In a podcast interview recorded around a year before the incident, he recalled that becoming a pilot was not a childhood ambition.After school, he initially enrolled in a textile engineering course because he expected to eventually contribute to his family's business.He later opted for a management course to prepare himself for the business.It was during that course, when he was just 19, that he attended an aviation seminar."Unlike a lot of other aviators right now, aviation was not like a childhood dream," Machchhar said in the interview.The seminar changed his plans.His decision to enter aviation initially worried his mother."My mom was scared," he recalled, explaining that commercial aviation was far less familiar to people around him 15-17 years ago. His father, however, was more comfortable with his decision.Machchhar subsequently completed his commercial pilot training in New Zealand before obtaining his Boeing 737 type rating at the Flight Safety Training Centre (FSTC) in Manesar, Gurgaon.Machchhar joined SpiceJet in 2011 and spent more than a decade with the airline, eventually becoming a senior commander and Line Training Captain.According to his professional profile, he accumulated more than 9,500 flying hours with SpiceJet, including over 6,400 hours as pilot-in-command. As a Line Training Captain, he was responsible for training, assessing and mentoring other pilots while ensuring adherence to operational and safety procedures.He moved to flydubai in June 2022 as a direct-entry captain and has since been flying the Boeing 737 fleet.His profile lists more than 9,750 hours of flying experience and experience on the Boeing 737-800 and Boeing 737 MAX 8/9.A senior pilot who had trained Machchhar previously described him as a "very decent and sober person" who was always willing to learn.Machchhar's brother is also a pilot with flydubai.The flydubai flight was carrying 174 passengers, including 166 Israeli citizens, when the incident unfolded.According to flight-tracking data, the Boeing 737 MAX descended from roughly 30,875 feet to 16,750 feet in just 29 seconds. Flightradar24 recorded an extreme descent rate of around 30,000 feet per minute.Reports said the Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with a knife. The captain was injured but managed to resist while the aircraft was in danger of losing control.Passengers and crew eventually entered the cockpit and subdued the attacker.The aircraft was then diverted and landed at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. Two additional pilots who had been travelling as passengers were also on board and later took over the aircraft.The severity of the descent surprised aviation experts. Former United Airlines pilot and aviation safety expert Steve Arroyo said he was surprised the aircraft remained intact after the extreme manoeuvre, while aviation investigator Jeff Guzzetti said the aircraft had enough altitude left for the pilots to recover.The aircraft also reportedly suffered damage to its rudder during the descent.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar managed to regain control of a flydubai aircraft after a co-pilot attacked him. The plane had dropped thousands of feet in a matter of seconds before passengers and crew intervened and the aircraft was eventually diverted to Saudi Arabia. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu later identified the captain and praised his actions.

Article Title: Why ‘kaun se wale papa’ remark led to man’s conviction
Article Text:
The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC (AI Image)

“Dekho papa aa gaye, don’t cry.”

“Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”





NEW DELHI: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark, “Kaun se wale papa?”, made when she told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Though the two had no prior dispute, the court held that the remark implied the woman had multiple partners and questioned the child’s paternity.Judicial magistrate first class Moksha Bains, in a Sept 24 judgment, said the remark was not an innocuous inquiry about the child’s father but carried an insinuation about the woman’s sexual propriety and fidelity. “The expression, when addressed to a woman in the aforesaid setting, is not an innocuous inquiry as to the identity of a person,” the judge observed, adding that its “obvious insinuation” was that there could be more than one man who could be described as the child’s father.The case dates back to March 23, 2021, when Priyanka Gupta was walking with her three-year-old daughter near RBI Enclave Gate in Paschim Vihar. As the child cried, Gupta told her,Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected,Gupta initially ignored the remark and, about two minutes later, handed over the child to her husband after he arrived in a car.She later informed her father-in-law, who called the police, following which an FIR was registered at Paschim Vihar East police station under Section 509 IPC.In his statement under Section 313 CrPC, Lal admitted making the remark but claimed it was not made with any “ill intention”. He also alleged false implication, with the defence arguing that Gupta wanted him removed from the street corner where he had run his ironing business for seven years.Rejecting the defence, the court observed: “The explanation offered by the accused that the words were spoken without ‘ill intention’ is a bare assertion. No surrounding circumstance has been brought on record from which the remark could reasonably acquire an innocent meaning.”The court said every rude or offensive remark addressed to a woman would not automatically constitute an offence under Section 509 IPC, as the insult must have the requisite nexus with her modesty. In this case, however, it held that the remark was personally directed at Gupta and made immediately after she referred to her child’s father, carrying a sexually derogatory insinuation concerning her relationship with men and the child’s paternity.The court held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted Lal under Section 509 IPC.
Article Summary: A Delhi court has convicted a man for insulting a woman’s modesty over a seemingly casual remark. Priyanka Gupta told her three-year-old daughter that her father had arrived to pick them up from school. Girdhari Lal, who ran a clothes ironing cart at a street corner, then allegedly interjected, “Kaun se wale papa aa gaye?”

Article Title: Hyderabad woman Sandhya Reddy becomes mayor of Sydney council
Article Text:
Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney





HYDERABAD: A Hyderabad-origin woman, Sandhya Reddy, was elected mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney, Australia, on Tuesday. According to members of the migrant community, she is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia.Affectionately known as Sandy, Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014 and was elected to the Strathfield Council as an independent councillor in 2021. In 2023, she was elected deputy mayor of the council.A lawyer by profession, Reddy was born and raised in Hyderabad, where she also pursued her education before moving to Australia in 2005. She has been living in the country ever since.Members of the Indian community in Australia hailed her achievement, describing it as both "symbolic and significant" for the country's multicultural communities.
Article Summary: Sandhya Reddy, originally from Hyderabad, has become the mayor of Strathfield Council in Sydney. She is the first Indian-born migrant woman to serve as a mayor in Australia. Reddy began her journey with the State Emergency Service in 2014.

Article Title: Jaipur man held for killing pregnant live-in partner, burying body in rented house courtyard
Article Text:
The murder came to light on Sept 27, (Representative Image)





JAIPUR: Police here Tuesday arrested a 20-year-old man for allegedly strangling his pregnant live-in partner and burying her body in the courtyard of their rented house in Prestige Garden Colony, Bindayaka.DCP (West) Prashant Kiran identified the accused as Pravesh Kumar alias Haggu. Police said he allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners.The murder came to light on Sept 27 when the house owner found Kiran’s body buried in the courtyard. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.During questioning, Kumar told police that he strangled Kiran with one hand and covered her nose and mouth with a cloth with the other. He initially tried to mislead investigators by claiming that Kiran had died by suicide and that he buried her body after panicking, police said.Kumar and Kiran had come to Jaipur from their village about two months ago. Kiran was pregnant and Kumar was living with her and taking care of her.The two used the same mobile phone. Kumar worked odd jobs to support them, police said.After the murder, Kumar allegedly switched off the phone and went to Samod on foot to visit the Hanuman temple.Police said he told them he went there to “wash away his sins”. He returned to work and stayed there from Sept 24 to 26.On Sept 27, after suspecting that the murder had been discovered, Kumar allegedly collected Rs 500 in wages from the factory owner and fled Jaipur.Police teams began searching for him after recovering Kiran’s body. Investigators examined CCTV footage, analysed technical evidence and prepared a route chart to track his movements.A police team eventually detained him on Agra-Lucknow Expressway and arrested him after questioning.Kumar is a resident of Parsa Auliya Lalpur village under Safdarganj police station in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Pravesh Kumar allegedly killed Kiran Rawat on Sept 23 after suspecting her of having an affair with another man. The two were related as nephew and aunt and had been living together as partners. Police said Kumar had poured about two kilograms of salt over the body before digging a pit and burying her.

Article Title: US government’s new order replaces ‘artificial intelligence’ with ‘Super Intelligence’; federal agencies directed to use new term
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump signs executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”

Why is Trump calling AI ‘ Super Intelligence ’

‘Super intelligence’ already has a different meaning in AI

Trump has been using the term for days

What does the name change mean for users

US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to stop using “artificial intelligence” and instead use the term “Super Intelligence”, or “SI”, in their official communications. The move comes as the Trump administration continues to push for rapid AI development while concerns grow over AI safety, job losses and autonomous systems acting without direct human control. The order says the new term better reflects what advanced AI systems can do and the opportunities they could create. Trump had already started using “Super Intelligence” in public remarks, including at the United Nations last week.The executive order says the technology has moved beyond simply copying or automating individual parts of human intelligence. “As these capabilities continue to improve, they increasingly represent not merely artificial intelligence, but a new era of Super Intelligence,” the order said. “It’s not artificial, we all agree on that,” Trump told reporters on Tuesday.The order directs federal agencies to use “Super Intelligence” or “SI” when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports, policy documents and other official material.It also gives Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, responsibility for deciding whether the government's definition of the term should be changed or expanded. “Within 60 days of the date of this order, the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST), in consultation with the heads of other agencies as the APST deems appropriate, shall submit to the President proposed legislative language to establish a Federal definition of “Super Intelligence” and “SI” that reflects the capabilities described in section 1 of this order,” the order stated.The term is not new to the AI industry. In AI research, superintelligence generally refers to a system that is more capable than humans across virtually all areas of cognitive work. Such a system has not been achieved.Trump's executive order uses the term more broadly for the rapidly developing AI technology being built today.This makes the change more than a simple wording update. Federal agencies will now be expected to use the administration's preferred terminology when discussing AI in their public-facing work.Trump began using “Super Intelligence” publicly before signing the executive order. During his address to the United Nations last week, he said the US would reject attempts to create a global system for controlling AI and referred to the technology as “Super Intelligence.”The White House has also used the term in its recent policy announcements. Following Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping, the two countries agreed to use “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” for the emerging technology. They also agreed to create a US-China Super Intelligence Dialogue to discuss its risks and benefits.The change in terminology comes as the debate over AI safety is becoming more intense. Trump has repeatedly argued that the US needs to remain ahead in AI development, particularly as it competes with China. His administration has also favoured working with AI companies rather than imposing broad new regulations.For most people, the immediate impact is likely to be limited. The executive order changes the terminology used by federal agencies rather than creating a new type of AI technology.Government websites, reports and policy documents will increasingly refer to “Super Intelligence” or “SI” instead of “artificial intelligence.” The administration says “Super Intelligence” better captures the rapid development and potential of AI. At the same time, AI companies and policymakers continue to debate how to prevent powerful systems from being misused or acting outside their intended purpose.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing federal agencies to stop using ‘artificial intelligence’ The order says the new term better reflects what advanced AI systems can do and the opportunities they could create. The move comes as the Trump administration continues to push for rapid AI development while concerns grow over AI safety.

Article Title: Less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit, the US government rules out working with China on AI; the American President says: Do not want ...
Article Text:
What Chinese President said on AI regulation

The US government has ruled out working with China on artificial intelligence. The US President Donald Trump made it clear that he does not want to cooperate with China on AI governance. Trump's reasoning is that it would help Beijing catch up with American companies. His comments come less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's high-profile US visit last week. The statement comes as pressure is mounting on the US administration to address risks posed by AI, after OpenAI and Anthropic reported that their AI agents had gone rogue and hacked into other companies' systems.Trump made the comments shortly before hosting AI executives for lunch at the White House. The American President told the audience that AI had come up only briefly in his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who visited Washington last week. “A lot of people say, let’s do it together with China, but then they’re going to be able to immediately gain access to things that we know that they don’t know,” Trump said. He added, “We’re leading now over China and everyone else, and I want to keep it that way. ”“Whoever wins AI ... whoever wins ‘SI,’ whoever wins super intelligence, wins.That’s the group that wins, and we’re leading now over China by a lot and everyone else, and we’re going to keep it that way,” Trump said in his address last week to the United Nations General Assembly. “I’m not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution — many say bigger than the Industrial Revolution or the internet itself — and we will be very careful,” he said.Incidentally, in contrast, Chinese President Xi, said during his US visit that AI must always remain under human control. “We have both the capability and responsibility to develop and manage AI for good and ensure that the development of AI is always under human control and serves the well-being of the people,” Xi said in the White House’s Grand Foyer.Earlier Tuesday, September 29, Trump unveiled America.gov, a website that features an AI-powered tool meant to serve as a “one-stop shop” for Americans navigating government services.The gathering at White House included a who’s who of the tech world, including Amodei, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Advanced Micro Devices CEO Lisa Su and OpenAI President Greg Brockman.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump made it clear that he does not want to cooperate with China on AI governance. Trump's reasoning is that it would help Beijing catch up with American companies. His comments come less than a week after Chinese President Xi Jinping's high-profile US visit last week.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai 'agrees' to the call that technology companies need to innovate responsibly; says: As I shared today ...
Article Text:
Photo: @RemporX/ X

What Google CEO Sundar Pichai said

What the accord actually says

Voluntary, not legally binding

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of AI development and governance do you think is most crucial? Robust internal processes Independent audits Board-level oversight 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a landmark agreement aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies to adopt safeguards while continuing to deliver economic and scientific benefits. Pichai revealed that Google has invested hundreds of billions of dollars in the past two years across its AI stack, with more spending planned. He emphasized that the company is focused on building products that deliver real value for people and businesses, while also investing in local communities and strengthening public trust in technology.In a post on X, Pichai described the meeting as an important conversation, confirming that Google had signed what he called the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. “Great to meet today with @POTUS, @JDVance, @SpeakerJohnsonand Administration + tech leaders. Important conversation and we signed today the White House Accord on Super Intelligence.As I shared today, Google has invested hundreds of billions in the last two years alone, with more to come, across the entire stack, to deliver benefits for America and the world.We’re working to build products that deliver real value for people and businesses, invest in local communities, and build trust in the technology.Industry also has to innovate responsibly. Google’s focused on building the right way, with appropriate testing, evaluations, red-teaming, and other safeguards against misuse and misalignment – and releasing models or products only after they’ve been thoroughly reviewed.We are committed to working with other industry leaders to establish norms and build public confidence. The White House Accord and the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities signed today is a solid basis for moving forward - it contains real tangible steps to promote safe development, while delivering the economic and scientific benefits of this technology,” wrote Pichai in a post on X.The full agreement is titled "The White House Accord on Superintelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier SI Responsibilities." Beyond Pichai, it was signed by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI founder Elon Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, alongside Trump himself.The one-page document lays out what's being described as a four-layer framework of controls and audits for frontier AI systems. The first layer requires companies to build robust internal processes to monitor their models during both training and deployment, ensuring systems behave as intended and that problems are identified and resolved quickly. Subsequent layers call for internal verification, partnerships with independent external auditors to assess whether safety controls are functioning as intended, and board-level oversight of the entire process.Despite its formal tone, House Speaker Mike Johnson was clear that the accord is entirely voluntary, and Trump himself described it as "morally" binding rather than legally enforceable, emphasizing that the industry will largely be left to police itself. At the signing event, Trump likened the document to a kind of constitution for AI governance, while Musk described the substance of the commitment as involving joint monitoring, special board committees, and companies essentially reviewing each other's safety practices.Zuckerberg struck a similarly measured tone afterward, calling the accord a reasonable starting point — one the broader industry could plausibly coalesce around going forward, rather than a finished framework.
Article Summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. The landmark agreement is aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies.

Article Title: Odisha police to groom teens as child marriage watchdogs
Article Text:
(Representative image) Odisha Police are implementing a three-day awareness drive to combat child marriage





BHUBANESWAR: To curb child marriage, Odisha Police have drawn up a strategy to groom adolescent students as crusaders against the social evil and encourage them to act as whistleblowers in their communities.Ahead of the International Day of the Girl Child on October 11, whose theme this year is “end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights”, all police stations across the state have been directed to conduct a three-day awareness drive from October 8. The programme will target students aged 14 to 18 in schools, hostels and residential educational institutions under their jurisdictions.The outreach campaign will be carried out under the aegis of Juventica, a child safety initiative launched by Odisha Police in May this year.“Police should engage with adolescents to develop them as potential leaders who can play an active role in preventing child marriages and addressing other child protection concerns in their families and neighbourhoods by reporting such incidents to the police,” a circular issued by the Crime Against Women and Children Wing (CAW&CW) to all SPs and DCPs on Wednesday stated.According to the 2011 Census, 28.8% of girls in Odisha were married before the legal age of 18.The prevalence declined to 21.3% in the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4), 20.5% in NFHS-5 and further to 18.6% in NFHS-6. However, the CAW&CW circular noted that the figure should be considered high in absolute terms.As part of the initiative, inspectors-in-charge of police stations, local Child Welfare Police Officers (CWPOs), women police personnel and Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) will jointly visit higher secondary schools, including residential institutions, to conduct awareness sessions.“The sessions will focus on the harmful effects of child marriage, including its impact on children’s physical and mental well-being, health risks associated with early and forced marriages, socio-economic consequences, and the legal penalties prescribed under the law,” a senior CAW&CW officer said.The latest initiative comes after Odisha Police directed Ama Police Samitis, the community policing committees functioning at the police station level, to identify children vulnerable to child marriage in five western Odisha districts — Sambalpur, Bargarh, Balangir, Jharsuguda and Subarnapur — which have reported a high incidence of underage marriages among girls.
Article Summary: Odisha Police are implementing a three-day awareness drive to combat child marriage. The programme will target students aged 14 to 18 in schools, hostels and residential educational institutions under their jurisdictions. The outreach campaign will be carried out under the aegis of Juventica.

Article Title: Javed Akhtar asks if Dadar residents will raise same noise concern over political jalsas after opposing CJP protest
Article Text:
Activists of the CJP and other civil society organisations are staging a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park

Shivaji Park residents oppose protest





MUMBAI: Lyricist Javed Akhtar quipped after residents of Shivaji Park objected to the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) protest at the venue, saying he was "hundred percent sure" that they would raise the same objection whenever a political party held a jalsa there.In a post on X, Akhtar said, "I am so happy that some residences of Shivaji park are getting sensitive about the noise pollution and asking the authorities to cancel the protest of CJP today at Shivaji park . I am hundred percent sure that they will raise the same objection with the same intensity if not more when ever there is any jalsa of any political party of Maharashtra is planned at Shivaji park."Activists of the CJP and other civil society organisations are staging a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park against the Election Commission and what they allege are irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process.Heavy police deployment was seen at Shivaji Park on Friday in view of the protest call.CJP spokesperson Saurav Das alleged that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar was a "traitor" and claimed that the whole country would support calls for his ouster."As you can see, we are starting from Mumbai today. This is going to be a very big protest. Mumbai showed last time what the spirit of Mumbai is. The youth of the whole country, the young generation, everyone came out last time for the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.""And this time too, it is going to be the same with Gyanesh Kumar, who is a traitor to the country. The youth of Mumbai are hitting the streets again. Today, a massive protest is going to happen at Shivaji Park. And I want, I appeal to all the Mumbaikars and our friends. Everyone come," Das said.A few residents of Shivaji Park have objected to the park being used as a protest site, citing inconvenience to people living in the area.Local resident Sunil Bhagwat, while talking to reporters, said people regularly visit Shivaji Park for walks and claimed that frequent protests were causing inconvenience to the common people.“We come here for walks in this park, but many protests have been happening here recently. Who is responsible for the troubles being caused to the common people? Did the Constitution not explain your duties towards the rest of the people? Who is responsible for the problems the common man here faces?” he said.Another resident, Ravindra, referred to the previous protest at the venue and said the crowd had reached Dadar Shivaji Park station and there were bottles of liquor thrown.“The previous time these people protested, they said that it was a spontaneous protest. There was such a huge crowd that it reached Dadar Shivaji Park station itself. Bottles of liquor were thrown at those who came here, and these people, the ones who call them ‘Jengi’, call them here by lying,” Ravindra said.He also raised concerns over the presence of schools and a hospital near the protest site, claiming that traffic movement had been affected during the previous protest.“There are two schools and a hospital here. Cars couldn’t pass through; around 5:00 PM, school was getting over and the school kids were stuck in their vehicles anyway. We all believe in the Constitution but the Constitution hasn’t given permission to these people, right? If the law and the Constitution haven’t granted permission, then what force are they using to come here?” he said.
Article Summary: Activists of the CJP and other civil society organisations are staging a protest at Mumbai's Shivaji Park. Lyricist Javed Akhtar quipped that he was "hundred percent sure" that they would raise the same objection whenever a political party held a jalsa there. Activists allege irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision process.

Article Title: Passenger deboarded after accidentally touching emergency exit door of flight at Hyderabad airport
Article Text:
(Representative image) A passenger was removed from a flight at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport after touching the emergency exit handle





HYDERABAD: A 35-year-old passenger was deboarded from a flight at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) after accidentally touching the aircraft’s emergency exit handle and triggering an alarm, according to news agency PTI.The incident took place on Thursday as the flight from Hyderabad to Kadapa was preparing for take-off.According to police, the passenger accidentally touched the emergency exit handle while adjusting his seat when the aircraft was stationary. The movement activated the door sensor alarm, following which airline staff deboarded him.The passenger was handed over to police for questioning. During the enquiry, police found that he had unintentionally touched the emergency exit.Police said they took a written statement from the passenger and allowed him to leave.No case was registered in connection with the incident.
Article Summary: A 35-year-old passenger was deboarded from a flight at Hyderabad's Rajiv Gandhi International Airport. The incident took place on Thursday as the flight from Hyderabad to Kadapa was preparing for take-off. The passenger was handed over to police for questioning.

Article Title: Delhi Jantar Mantar protest: Section 163 in force, 11 Metro stations closed, traffic curbs announced; what commuters need to know
Article Text:
Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest and deployed additional security personnel in and around New Delhi, officials said.

Section 163 BNSS order in force in New Delhi

11 Delhi Metro stations to remain closed

The affected stations are:

Janpath

Patel Chowk

Central Secretariat

Rajiv Chowk

Seva Teerth

Mandi House

Lok Kalyan Marg

INA

Chawri Bazar

Ramakrishna Ashram Marg

New Delhi

Traffic restrictions, diversions around Jantar Mantar

Security beefed up ahead of protest





NEW DELHI: Security has been stepped up in New Delhi ahead of a proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar at Jantar Mantar on Friday, with Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in force and restrictions imposed on Metro and road movement in the area.Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest and deployed additional security personnel in and around New Delhi, officials said. The protest is being called by the All India Students' Association (AISA), Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha and Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan and is scheduled to begin at 11 am."Permission has not been granted for any type of protest, march at Jantar Mantar and preventive measures have been taken. I would request everyone to abide by the law and cooperate with the police. Section 163 is in force here. Section 163 of the BNSS is in force in New Delhi. Therefore, I am making it clear that no unauthorised sit-in, protest or demonstration is allowed here. I request everyone to follow the law, be law-abiding and cooperate with the police, " DCP Sachin Sharma told news agency PTI.Police sources said around 3,000 to 4,000 people were expected to attend the gathering, prompting heightened security arrangements in the area.A prohibitory order under Section 163 of the BNSS, 2023, is in force in New Delhi district to ensure public safety, maintain public order and facilitate smooth traffic movement.Under the order, public meetings or assemblies of five or more persons, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas are prohibited without prior written permission.Shouting slogans or making speeches is also prohibited without prior written permission. The order further prohibits carrying firearms, banners, placards, lathis, swords, sticks, brickbats or similar articles.Citizens, visitors and all stakeholders have been advised to strictly comply with the order and refrain from any unauthorised gathering or prohibited activity.Violation of the order shall invite legal action under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, and other applicable provisions of law.Entry and exit at 11 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed till further notice. However, interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, New Delhi and Central Secretariat stations.Delhi Traffic Police has also issued a traffic advisory for October 2, warning commuters of restrictions and regulated movement around Jantar Mantar and adjoining areas.Traffic diversions and regulations will be in place around Connaught Place, Patel Chowk, GPO, Tolstoy Marg, Jantar Mantar Road, Parliament Street and adjoining roads.Traffic from Connaught Place towards Patel Chowk will be diverted through alternate routes as directed by traffic personnel, while movement from Patel Chowk towards GPO will be regulated or diverted at appropriate points.Traffic movement on Tolstoy Marg will also be regulated or diverted, with commuters advised to avoid the stretch wherever possible. Movement on Jantar Mantar Road will be restricted or diverted, and motorists have been advised to use alternate routes.The traffic police has advised the public to avoid Jantar Mantar, Parliament Street, Ashoka Road and adjoining roads wherever possible.Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) personnel have been deployed alongside Delhi Police teams at Jantar Mantar and other key points in New Delhi district.Barricades have been put up and additional personnel positioned at entry and exit points and other sensitive locations to regulate movement and prevent any unauthorised gathering, police sources said.The organisers are seeking the resignation or impeachment of Kumar, alleging irregularities in electoral rolls and the conduct of elections. They have also raised concerns over the Election Commission's handling of electoral rolls and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, claiming it raises questions over the protection of citizens' voting rights.AAP leaders and workers, members of the Indian Youth Congress and others are expected to participate in the protest, sources said.Delhi Police's decision came a day after AISA national president Neha Bora, Bhushan and Jha announced the proposed gathering at a press conference.Bora said the organisers had informed the Parliament Street police station about the gathering, including the expected turnout, timing and details of those responsible for organising it.The proposed protest comes amid demonstrations by opposition parties, student groups and civil society activists in Delhi over the functioning of the poll panel and the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has denied permission for the proposed protest and deployed additional security personnel in and around New Delhi. The protest is being called by the All India Students' Association (AISA), Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha and Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan. Police sources said around 3,000 to 4,000 people were expected to attend the gathering.
